mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing liquidity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following low FEDFUNDS levels, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate signals economic weakness, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer spending and business investment decline over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows following a significant rise in UNRATE, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment (UNRATE) increase simultaneously, it indicates a tightening labor market, which may lead to inflationary pressures and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following simultaneous increases in PAYEMS and UNRATE, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand in the housing market, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns as related industries benefit over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 20-day windows following a significant increase in HOUST, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests strong economic activity, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings improve over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 5-day windows following an increase in INDPRO, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A high consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicates inflationary pressures, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as the Federal Reserve may tighten monetary policy over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows following a high CPIAUCSL, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both GDP (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) increase, it indicates strong economic growth, which may lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 30% of the 60-day windows following simultaneous increases in GDPC1 and RSAFS, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates a tightening monetary policy, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs increase and liquidity decreases over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following a rise in FEDFUNDS, this hypothesis is rejected.
